196.subject: Botany
196.text: What happens to a cell during M phase of cell cycle?
196.sol: During $G_1$ phase, the cell is in resting state and the nucleocytoplasmic index is stable. During the $\mathrm{S}$ phase of the cell cycle, DNA replicates, consequently nucleocytoplasmic index increases due to increase in nuclear volume. During $G_2$ phase, the cell is again stable. During M phase, nucleocytoplasmic index decreases. After $M$ phase or mitosis when the cell divides, nucleoplasmic index returns to normal.
196.meta: What happens to a cell during M phase of cell cycle?

1289.subject: Physics
1289.text:
Assertion : Television signals are received through sky-wave propagation.
Reason : The ionosphere reflects electromagnetic waves of frequencies greater than a certain critical frequency.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1289.sol:
In sky wave propagation, the radio waves having frequency range $2 \mathrm{MHz}$ to $30 \mathrm{MHz}$ are reflected back by the ionosphere. Radio waves having frequency nearly greater than $30 \mathrm{MHz}$ penetrates the ionosphere and is not reflected back by the ionosphere. The TV signal having frequency greater than $30 \mathrm{MHz}$ therefore cannot be propagated through sky wave propagation.
In case of sky wave propagation, critical frequency is defined as the highest frequency that is returned to the earth by the considered layer of the ionosphere after having sent straight to it. Above this frequency, a wave will penetrate the ionosphere and is not reflected by it.

1677.text: A particle is thrown vertically up with an initial velocity $9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ from the surface of Earth (take $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ). The time (in s) taken by the particle to reach a height of $4 \mathrm{~m}$ from the surface second time (in seconds) is
1677.sol:
Time taken by the particle to reach a height $h$ from the surface of Earth is obtained from $h=u t-\frac{1}{2} g t^2$
Here, $u=9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, h=4 \mathrm{~m}, g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad 4=9 t-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \\ & 4=9 t-5 t^2 \quad \text{$ or $} 5 t^2-9 t+4=0 \\ & 5 t^2-5 t-4 t+4=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 5 t(t-1)-4(t-1)=0 \\ & \therefore \quad t=1 \mathrm{~s} \text{ or } t=\frac{4}{5} \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$
Hence, the time taken by the particle to reach a height of $4 \mathrm{~m}$ from the surface second time is $1 \mathrm{~s}$.

Surface area of sphere $(S)=4 \pi r^2$ $$ \frac{d S}{d t}=4 \pi(2 r) \cdot \frac{d r}{d t} $$
Eq. (i) divided by Eq. (ii), we get $$ \begin{array}{ll} \frac{\frac{d V}{d t}}{\frac{d S}{d t}}=\frac{4 \pi r^2 \cdot \frac{d r}{d t}}{8 \pi r \cdot \frac{d r}{d t}} & \\ \frac{d V}{d S}=\frac{r}{2}=\frac{10}{2} & {[\because r=10 \mathrm{~cm}]} \\ \frac{d V}{d S}=5 \mathrm{~cm} & \end{array} $$ Hence, option (d) is correct.

15990.text: Position of a $2 \mathrm{ kg}$ mass moving along the $X$-axis is given by $x=2 \cos [(2) t] \mathrm{m}$. Then maximum kinetic energy of the mass in joule is
15990.sol:
Position of particle, $x=2 \cos (2 t)\Rightarrow$ Velocity of particle, $v=\frac{d x}{d t}=\frac{d}{d t} 2 \cos 2 t\Rightarrow \quad v=-2 \sin 2 t \times \frac{d}{d t} 2 t \Rightarrow v=-4 \sin 2 t$
Velocity is maximum when $\sin 2 t=1$. Hence maximum kinetic energy of particle is
$K_{\max }=\frac{1}{2} m\left(v_{\max }\right)^2$
Substituting $m=2 \mathrm{ kg}$ and $v_{\max }=-4 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$;
$\Rightarrow \quad K_{\max }=\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times(-4)^2=16 \mathrm{ J}$

19625.text:
What would be the final product [$\mathrm{X}$] formed when p-Toluidine undergoes the following series of reactions?
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ P-Toluidine } \xrightarrow[\text{ Pyridine }]{\left\{\mathrm{CH}_2, \mathrm{CO}_2 \mathrm{O}\right.}[\mathrm{P}] \\
& {[\mathrm{P}] \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br}_2 / \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}}[\mathrm{O}]} \\
& {[\mathrm{Q}] \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{ dilÐ½G }}[\mathrm{R}]} \\
& {\mathrm{[R]} \xrightarrow[0^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}]{\mathrm{Nan}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}}\mathrm{[S]}} \\
& {[\mathrm{S}] \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{PO}_2}[\mathrm{X}]} \\
\end{aligned}$
19625.sol:
The starting material is p-toluidine (4-methylaniline).

Reaction with acetic anhydride in pyridine protects the amino group as an acetanilide derivative, forming p-methylacetanilide [P].

Bromination of p-methylacetanilide with $Br_2/CH_3COOH$ occurs at the ortho position relative to the amino group (which is the position ortho to the $-NHCOCH_3$ group and meta to the $-CH_3$ group), yielding 2-bromo-4-methylacetanilide [Q].

Hydrolysis of the acetamido group in dilute acid with heating yields 2-bromo-4-methylaniline [R].

Diazotization of [R] with $NaNO_2/HCl$ at $0^{{}^{\circ}}C$ converts the amino group into a diazonium salt, 2-bromo-4-methylbenzenediazonium chloride [S].

Reduction of the diazonium salt with $H_3PO_2$ (hypophosphorous acid) removes the diazonium group, resulting in 2-bromotoluene [X].

Comparing this structure with the given options, the product is 2-bromotoluene, which corresponds to the image provided in option (4).

19751.subject: Chemistry
19751.text: Given are 4 pairs of covalent molecules. Identify the pair in which both molecules have the same shape.
19751.sol:
The shape of a molecule is determined by the arrangement of its atoms, which depends on the number of bonding pairs and lone pairs around the central atom according to VSEPR theory.

For $\mathrm{BF}_3$, the central atom B has 3 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, resulting in a trigonal planar geometry. For $\mathrm{NH}_3$, the central atom N has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, resulting in a trigonal pyramidal geometry. They have different shapes.

For $\mathrm{XeF}_4$, the central atom Xe has 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs, resulting in a square planar geometry. For $\mathrm{SF}_4$, the central atom S has 4 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, resulting in a see-saw geometry. They have different shapes.

For $\mathrm{XeF}_2$, the central atom Xe has 2 bonding pairs and 3 lone pairs, resulting in a linear geometry. For $\mathrm{HgCl}_2$, the central atom Hg has 2 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, resulting in a linear geometry. Both molecules have the same shape.

For $\mathrm{BrF}_5$, the central atom Br has 5 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, resulting in a square pyramidal geometry. For $\mathrm{PCl}_5$, the central atom P has 5 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, resulting in a trigonal bipyramidal geometry. They have different shapes.

Answer: $\mathrm{XeF}_2\ \text{ and } \mathrm{HgCl}_2$

19854.subject: Chemistry
19854.text: In the synthesis of NH_3$ from H_2$ and N_2$, if 6 \times 10^{-2}$ mole of hydrogen disappears in 10 minutes, the number of moles of NH_3$ formed in 0.3 minutes is:$
19854.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the synthesis of ammonia is:

$N_2 + 3H_2 \rightarrow 2NH_3$

The rate of disappearance of $H_2$ is given by:

$-\dfrac{d[H_2]}{dt} = \dfrac{6 \times 10^{-2}}{10} = 6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol min}^{-1}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, the rate of formation of $NH_3$ is related to the rate of disappearance of $H_2$ as:

$\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{d[NH_3]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{3} \dfrac{d[H_2]}{dt}$

$\dfrac{d[NH_3]}{dt} = -\dfrac{2}{3} \dfrac{d[H_2]}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 6 \times 10^{-3} = 4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol min}^{-1}$

The number of moles of $NH_3$ formed in $0.3$ minutes is:

$\text{Moles of } NH_3 = \text{Rate} \times \text{Time} = 4 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.3 = 1.2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ moles}$

19932.subject: Chemistry
19932.text: $a P+b Q \longrightarrow$ products, when $[P]$ is doubled keeping $[Q]$ constant and rate increases 2 times, when $[P]$ is constant and $[Q]$ is doubled and rate increases four times. The overall order is
19932.sol:
For a reaction,
$a P+b Q \rightarrow$ Products
$r=k[P]^{a}[Q]^{b} \quad \text{...(i)}2 r=k[2 P]^{a}[Q]^{b} \quad \text{...(ii)}4 r=k[P]^{a}[2 Q]^{b} \quad \text{...(iii)}$
On dividing Eqs. (ii) by (i), we get 2=2^{a} \Rightarrow a=1 On dividing Eqs. (iii) by (i), we get 4=2^{b} \Rightarrow b=2 $\therefore$ Overall order $=a+b=1+2=3$.

20078.subject: Chemistry
20078.sol:
The reaction sequence describes the industrial preparation of potassium dichromate from chromite ore. The compound W is chromite ore, $\mathrm{FeCr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$.

In the first step, chromite ore reacts with sodium carbonate in the presence of air (oxygen) to form sodium chromate:
$4\mathrm{FeCr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4} + 8\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CO}_{3} + 7\mathrm{O}_{2} \rightarrow 8\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4} + 2\mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3} + 8\mathrm{CO}_{2}$

Here, X is $\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}$. Upon acidification with $\mathrm{H}^{+}$, sodium chromate converts to sodium dichromate:
$2\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4} + 2\mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7} + 2\mathrm{Na}^{+} + \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

The resulting sodium dichromate (Y) reacts with potassium chloride (KCl) to form potassium dichromate (Z), which appears as orange crystals:
$\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7} + 2\mathrm{KCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7} + 2\mathrm{NaCl}$

Potassium dichromate is a well-known strong oxidizing agent in acidic medium.

Answer: $\mathrm{FeCr}_2 \mathrm{O}_4$

20133.subject: Chemistry
20133.text:
What is the standard electrode potential at 298 K for the reaction: $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+1 \mathrm{e}-\rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{+1}$ ?
Given: $\mathrm{E}_0 \mathrm{Cu}^{+1} / \mathrm{Cu}=0.5 \mathrm{ V} \quad \ \text{ and } \quad \mathrm{E}_0 \mathrm{Cu}^{+2} / \mathrm{Cu}=0.335 \mathrm{ V}$
20133.sol:
The standard electrode potential for the reaction $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + \mathrme^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ can be determined using the Gibbs free energy change $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}} = -nFE^{{}^{\circ}}$.

For the reaction $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + 2\mathrme^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{1} = -2 \times F \times 0.335 = -0.67F$.

For the reaction $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} + \mathrme^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{2} = -1 \times F \times 0.5 = -0.5F$.

The target reaction is $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + \mathrme^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{+}$, which is obtained by subtracting the second reaction from the first:

$\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{3} = \Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{1} - \Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{2} = -0.67F - (-0.5F) = -0.17F$.

Since $\Delta G^{{}^{\circ}}_{3} = -nFE^{{}^{\circ}}_{3}$ with $n=1$, we have $-1 \times F \times E^{{}^{\circ}}_{3} = -0.17F$.

Therefore, $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{3} = 0.17 \text{ V}$.

Answer: 0.17 V

20228.subject: Chemistry
20228.text: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Staggered conformation of ethane is more stable than the eclipsed conformation.
The energy difference between the staggered and eclipsed conformation of ethane is $12.55 \mathrm{ kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$
A $90^{{}^{\circ}}$ rotation converts staggered conformation of ethane into eclipsed conformation.
The distance between non-bonded H-atoms of ethane in eclipsed conformation is $2.29 Å$
20228.sol:
In the ethane molecule, the staggered conformation is more stable than the eclipsed conformation due to lower torsional strain. This is a correct statement.

The energy difference between the staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane is approximately $12.55 \text{ kJ/mol}$ ($3.0 \text{ kcal/mol}$), which is a correct statement.

The dihedral angle between the C-H bonds of adjacent carbon atoms in the staggered conformation is $60^{{}^{\circ}}$. A rotation of $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ about the C-C bond converts the staggered conformation into the eclipsed conformation. Therefore, a $90^{{}^{\circ}}$ rotation does not convert the staggered conformation into the eclipsed conformation. This is an incorrect statement.

In the eclipsed conformation of ethane, the distance between the non-bonded hydrogen atoms on adjacent carbon atoms is approximately $2.29 \text{ \AA}$, which is a correct statement.

Answer: A $90^{{}^{\circ}}$ rotation converts staggered conformation of ethane into eclipsed conformation.

21131.subject: Mathematics
21131.text: The circle $x^2+y^2+4 x-7 y+12=0$ cuts an intercept on $Y$-axis of length
21131.sol:
The equation of the circle is $x^2 + y^2 + 4x - 7y + 12 = 0$.

To find the intercept on the Y-axis, set $x = 0$ in the equation of the circle.

$0^2 + y^2 + 4(0) - 7y + 12 = 0$

$y^2 - 7y + 12 = 0$

Factoring the quadratic equation, we get $(y - 3)(y - 4) = 0$.

The roots are $y_1 = 3$ and $y_2 = 4$.

The length of the intercept on the Y-axis is $|y_2 - y_1| = |4 - 3| = 1$.

Answer: 1

21292.subject: Mathematics
21292.text: If $A=\left[\begin{array}{cc}2-k & 2 \\ 1 & 3-k\end{array}\right]$ is a singular matrix, then the value of $5 k-k^2$ is
21292.sol:
A matrix $A$ is singular if its determinant is zero, so $\det(A) = 0$.

Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2-k & 2 \\ 1 & 3-k \end{bmatrix}$, the determinant is calculated as:

$\det(A) = (2-k)(3-k) - (2)(1) = 0$

Expanding the expression:

$6 - 2k - 3k + k^2 - 2 = 0$

$k^2 - 5k + 4 = 0$

Rearranging the terms to find the value of $5k - k^2$:

$k^2 - 5k = -4$

Multiplying by $-1$ gives:

$5k - k^2 = 4$

Answer: 4

21343.subject: Mathematics
21343.text: $\text{ The general solution of the differential equation }(1+\tan y)(d x-d y)+2 x d y=0 \text{$ is }
21343.sol:
The given differential equation is $(1+\tan y)(dx - dy) + 2x dy = 0$.

Rearranging the terms to form a linear differential equation in $x$:

$(1+\tan y) dx = (1+\tan y - 2x) dy$

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1+\tan y - 2x}{1+\tan y} = 1 - \dfrac{2x}{1+\tan y}$

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} + \left(\dfrac{2}{1+\tan y}\right) x = 1$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dx}{dy} + P(y)x = Q(y)$, where $P(y) = \dfrac{2}{1+\tan y} = \dfrac{2\cos y}{\cos y + \sin y}$.

The integrating factor (IF) is $e^{\int P(y) dy} = e^{\int \dfrac{2\cos y}{\sin y + \cos y} dy}$.

Let $I = \int \dfrac{2\cos y}{\sin y + \cos y} dy$. Note that $2\cos y = (\cos y + \sin y) + (\cos y - \sin y)$.

$I = \int \left(1 + \dfrac{\cos y - \sin y}{\sin y + \cos y}\right) dy = y + \ln|\sin y + \cos y|$.

Thus, $IF = e^{y + \ln|\sin y + \cos y|} = e^y (\sin y + \cos y)$.

The solution is $x(IF) = \int Q(y)(IF) dy + c$.

$x e^y (\sin y + \cos y) = \int e^y (\sin y + \cos y) dy + c$.

Using integration by parts on $\int e^y (\sin y + \cos y) dy$:

Let $f(y) = \sin y + \cos y$, then $f'(y) = \cos y - \sin y$. This does not immediately simplify, but $\int e^y (\sin y + \cos y) dy = e^y \sin y + c$.

Therefore, $x e^y (\sin y + \cos y) = e^y \sin y + c$.

Dividing by $e^y$, we get $x(\sin y + \cos y) = \sin y + c e^{-y}$.

Answer: $x(\sin y+\cos y)=\sin y+c e^{-y}$

21520.subject: Mathematics
21520.text: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{d y}{d x}-y=1$ given $y(0)=1$, is
21520.sol:
The given differential equation is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$, where $P = -1$ and $Q = 1$.

The integrating factor (IF) is given by $IF = e^{\int P dx} = e^{\int -1 dx} = e^{-x}$.

Multiplying both sides of the differential equation by the integrating factor, we get $e^{-x} \dfrac{dy}{dx} - e^{-x} y = e^{-x}$, which can be written as $\dfrac{d}{dx}(y e^{-x}) = e^{-x}$.

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we have $y e^{-x} = \int e^{-x} dx = -e^{-x} + C$.

Multiplying by $e^x$, we obtain $y = -1 + C e^x$.

Using the initial condition $y(0) = 1$, we substitute $x = 0$ and $y = 1$: $1 = -1 + C e^0 \Rightarrow 1 = -1 + C \Rightarrow C = 2$.

Substituting $C = 2$ into the general solution, we get $y = 2 e^x - 1$.

Answer: $y=2 e^x-1$

21572.subject: Mathematics
21572.sol:
Let $I = \int \dfrac{4^x}{\sqrt{1-16^x}} dx$.

Rewrite the integral as $I = \int \dfrac{4^x}{\sqrt{1-(4^x)^2}} dx$.

Substitute $u = 4^x$. Then $du = 4^x \ln 4 dx$, which implies $4^x dx = \dfrac{du}{\ln 4}$.

Substituting these into the integral gives $I = \int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^2}} \cdot \dfrac{du}{\ln 4}$.

$I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 4} \int \dfrac{du}{\sqrt{1-u^2}}$.

Using the standard integral $\int \dfrac{du}{\sqrt{1-u^2}} = \sin^{-1} u + C$, we get $I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 4} \sin^{-1} u + C$.

Substituting back $u = 4^x$, we obtain $I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 4} \sin^{-1} 4^x + C$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\log 4} \sin ^{-1} 4^x+C$

21608.subject: Mathematics
21608.text: The value of the expression $\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right) + \sin^{-1}\left(\sin\dfrac{22\pi}{3}\right) + \tan^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{4\pi}{5}\right)$ is:
21608.sol:
The principal value branch of $\cos^{-1}x$ is $[0, \pi]$.

$\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right) = \cos^{-1}\left(\cos\left(2\pi - \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\right) = \cos^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$

The principal value branch of $\sin^{-1}x$ is $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

$\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\dfrac{22\pi}{3}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\sin\left(7\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(-\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

The principal value branch of $\tan^{-1}x$ is $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

$\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{4\pi}{5}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\tan\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{5}\right)\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(-\tan\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{5}$

Adding the three values:

$\dfrac{5\pi}{6} - \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{5} = \dfrac{25\pi - 10\pi - 6\pi}{30} = \dfrac{9\pi}{30} = \dfrac{3\pi}{10}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3\pi}{10}$

22034.subject: Mathematics
22034.text:
If $A = \{x : x\ \text{is the first three odd numbers}\}$
$B = \{2x + 3 : 0 \leq x < 5, x \in \mathbb{N}\}$, then which of the following is true
22034.sol:
The first three odd natural numbers are $1, 3$, and $5$.

$A = \{1, 3, 5\}$

For set $B$, the condition is $0 \leq x < 5$ and $x \in \mathbb{N}$. The natural numbers satisfying this condition are $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$.

Substituting these values into $2x + 3$:
For $x = 1$, $2(1) + 3 = 5$
For $x = 2$, $2(2) + 3 = 7$
For $x = 3$, $2(3) + 3 = 9$
For $x = 4$, $2(4) + 3 = 11$

$B = \{5, 7, 9, 11\}$

Finding the intersection of sets $A$ and $B$:

$A \cap B = \{1, 3, 5\} \cap \{5, 7, 9, 11\} = \{5\}$

Since $A \cap B$ contains exactly one element, it is a singleton set. Also, $n(B) = 4$.

Answer: $A \cap B$ is a singleton set

23609.subject: Physics
23609.text: The dimension $[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{ T}^{-2}]$ is the physical quantity of
23609.sol:
The given dimension is $[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Pressure is defined as $\dfrac{\text{Force}}{\text{Area}} = \dfrac{[M L T^{-2}]}{[L^2]} = [M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Energy density is defined as $\dfrac{\text{Energy}}{\text{Volume}} = \dfrac{[M L^2 T^{-2}]}{[L^3]} = [M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Since both Pressure and Energy density have the dimension $[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$, we evaluate the options provided.

Option (1) Energy density has the dimension $[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$.

Option (2) Pressure $\times$ Area is Force, which has dimension $[M L T^{-2}]$.

Option (3) Power $\times$ Time is Energy, which has dimension $[M L^2 T^{-2}]$.

Option (4) $\dfrac{\text{Force}}{\text{Pressure}}$ is Area, which has dimension $[L^2]$.

Therefore, Energy density is the correct physical quantity.

Answer: Energy density

26054.subject: Physics
26054.text:
Passage: A container of height $2$ m, length $2$ m and breadth $1$ m is made of insulating vertical walls and two large area horizontal metal plates ($M_1$ and $M_2$) which extend far beyond the vertical walls in all directions. The container is partitioned into two equal chambers with a thin insulating vertical wall. The partition wall contains a small hole of cross-sectional area $\sqrt{10}$ cm$^2$ near its bottom edge. Initially the hole is closed and the left chamber of the container is completely filled with a liquid of dielectric constant $\epsilon_r = 15$ and the right chamber is empty ($\epsilon_r = 1$). At time $t = 0$, the hole is opened and the liquid flows from the left chamber to the right chamber. In both the chambers, the space above the liquid has $\epsilon_r = 1$ and is maintained at atmospheric pressure. The schematic of the container at a time $t > 0$ is shown in the figure.
[Given: acceleration due to gravity is $10$ ms$^{-2}$.]


Question: The difference in the capacitance (in F) between the metal plates at $t = 0$ and that at $t = 500$ s is $(8 - n)\epsilon_0$, where $\epsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space. The value of $n$ is:
26054.sol:
Let $A$ be the area of each chamber. $A = 1 \times 1 = 1 \text{ m}^2$. Distance between plates is $d = 2 \text{ m}$.

At $t = 0$, the left chamber is completely filled with liquid ($\epsilon_r = 15$) and right chamber is empty ($\epsilon_r = 1$).

Initial capacitance $C(0) = C_1 + C_2 = \dfrac{15 \epsilon_0 A}{d} + \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d} = \dfrac{15 \epsilon_0 (1)}{2} + \dfrac{\epsilon_0 (1)}{2} = 8 \epsilon_0$.

Let $y_1$ and $y_2$ be the liquid levels in the left and right chambers at time $t$. By conservation of volume, $y_1 + y_2 = 2 \text{ m}$.

Let $h = y_1 - y_2$. The velocity of efflux from the left chamber is $v = \sqrt{2gh}$.

Rate of flow $Q = -A \dfrac{dy_1}{dt} = a \sqrt{2gh}$, where $a = \sqrt{10} \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$ is the hole area.

Since $y_1 + y_2 = 2$, we have $dy_2 = -dy_1$, so $dh = 2dy_1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy_1}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{dh}{dt}$.

$-\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{dh}{dt} = a \sqrt{2gh} \Rightarrow \dfrac{dh}{\sqrt{h}} = -2a \sqrt{2g} dt$.

Integrating from $t=0$ ($h=2$) to $t=500 \text{ s}$ ($h$):

$\int_{2}^{h} h^{-1/2} dh = -2a \sqrt{2g} \int_{0}^{500} dt$

$2\sqrt{h} - 2\sqrt{2} = -2 (\sqrt{10} \times 10^{-4}) (\sqrt{20}) (500) = -\sqrt{200} \times 10^{-4} \times 1000 = -10\sqrt{2} \times 0.1 = -\sqrt{2}$.

$2\sqrt{h} = \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow \sqrt{h} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow h = 0.5 \text{ m}$.

From $y_1 + y_2 = 2$ and $y_1 - y_2 = 0.5$, we get $y_1 = 1.25 \text{ m}$ and $y_2 = 0.75 \text{ m}$.

At $t=500 \text{ s}$, each chamber acts as two capacitors in series (liquid and air).

$C_{left} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{y_1}{15\epsilon_0 A} + \dfrac{2-y_1}{\epsilon_0 A}} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{30 - 14y_1} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{30 - 14(1.25)} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{12.5} = \dfrac{6}{5} \epsilon_0 = 1.2 \epsilon_0$.

$C_{right} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{y_2}{15\epsilon_0 A} + \dfrac{2-y_2}{\epsilon_0 A}} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{30 - 14y_2} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{30 - 14(0.75)} = \dfrac{15\epsilon_0}{19.5} = \dfrac{150}{195} \epsilon_0 = \dfrac{10}{13} \epsilon_0$.

$C(500) = C_{left} + C_{right} = \dfrac{6}{5} \epsilon_0 + \dfrac{10}{13} \epsilon_0 = \dfrac{128}{65} \epsilon_0 \approx 1.97 \epsilon_0$.

Difference in capacitance $= C(0) - C(500) = 8\epsilon_0 - \dfrac{128}{65}\epsilon_0 = \left(8 - \dfrac{128}{65}\right)\epsilon_0$.

Comparing this with the given expression $(8 - n)\epsilon_0$, we get $n = \dfrac{128}{65} = 1.97$

For example, the phase space diagram for a particle moving with constant velocity is a straight line as shown in the figure. 26453.text: In a radioactive sample, ${}_{19}^{40}K$ nuclei either decay into stable ${}_{20}^{40}Ca$ nuclei with decay constant $4.5 \times {10}^{- 10}$ per year or into stable ${}_{18}^{40}Ar$ nuclei with decay constant $0.5 \times {10}^{- 10}$ per year. Given that in this sample all the stable ${}_{20}^{40}Ca$ and ${}_{18}^{40}Ar$ nuclei are produced by the ${}_{19}^{40}K$ nuclei only. In time $t \times {10}^{9}$ years, if the ratio of the sum of stable ${}_{20}^{40}Ca$ and ${}_{18}^{40}Ar$ nuclei to the radioactive ${}_{19}^{40}K$ nuclei is $99,$ the value of t will be : [Given $ln10 = 2.3$ ]
26453.sol:
Given that, ${}_{19}^{49}K$ decays in two stable ${}_{20}^{40}Caof{}_{18}^{40}Ar$ Nuclei. Let there be ${N}_{0}$ active nuclei of ${}_{19}^{40}K$ present at $t = 0$ and none of ${}_{20}^{40}Ca and {}_{18}^{40}Ar$ present of $t = 0$ .
Where ${\lambda}_{1}$ (decay constant for $K \to Ca$ ) $= 4.5 \times \dfrac{{10}^{- 10}}{year}$ and
${\lambda}_{2}$ (decay constant for $K \to Ar$ ) $= 0.5 \times \dfrac{{10}^{- 10}}{year}$
These form two parallel nuclear reactions.
$∴$ Equivalent decay consent, $\lambda = {\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2} = 5 \times \dfrac{{10}^{- 10}}{year}$
Now, number of active nuclei of ${}_{19}^{40}K$ left at $\left(t = t\right) = N$
And according to Law of Radioactivity,
$N = {N}_{0}{e}^{- \lambdat}$ ........(i)
Now, according to question,
$\dfrac{{N}_{0} - N}{N} = 99 ⇒ {N}_{0} = 100N ⇒ N = \dfrac{{N}_{0}}{100}$
Then using equation (i)
$\dfrac{{N}_{0}}{100} = {N}_{0}{e}^{- \lambdat}$
$⇒ ln100 = \lambdat ⇒ t = \dfrac{2ln10}{\lambda} = \dfrac{2 \times 2.3}{5 \times {10}^{- 10}} = 9.2 \times {10}^{10}years$

27706.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The number of species among $\mathrm{BF}_{4}{ }^{-}, \mathrm{SiF}_{4}, \mathrm{XeF}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{SF}_{4}$, that have unequal $\mathrm{E}-\mathrm{F}$ bond lengths is two. Here, E is the central atom.
Statement II: Among $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{-}, \mathrm{O}_{2}{ }^{2-}, \mathrm{F}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{O}_{2}{ }^{+}, \mathrm{O}_{2}^{-}$has the highest bond order.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
27706.sol:
Statement I: Let's analyze the geometry of the given species.
$BF_4^-$: $sp^3$ hybridization, tetrahedral geometry. All B-F bond lengths are equal.
$SiF_4$: $sp^3$ hybridization, tetrahedral geometry. All Si-F bond lengths are equal.
$XeF_4$: $sp^3d^2$ hybridization, square planar geometry. All Xe-F bond lengths are equal.
$SF_4$: $sp^3d$ hybridization, see-saw geometry. It has axial and equatorial bonds. Axial bonds are longer than equatorial bonds due to greater repulsion. Thus, only $SF_4$ has unequal bond lengths. The number of species is one, not two. Statement I is false.
Statement II: Bond order calculation using Molecular Orbital Theory:
Total electrons in $O_2^-$ = 17, Bond Order = 1.5
Total electrons in $O_2^{2-}$ = 18, Bond Order = 1.0
Total electrons in $F_2$ = 18, Bond Order = 1.0
Total electrons in $O_2^+$ = 15, Bond Order = 2.5
Among these, $O_2^+$ has the highest bond order (2.5), not $O_2^-$. Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

28521.subject: Chemistry
28521.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
28521.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement - I: Along the period, the chemical reactivity of the element gradually increases from group $1$ to group $18$ .
Statement - II: The nature of oxides formed by group $1$ element is basic while that of group $17$ elements is acidic.
In the the light above statements, choose the most appropriate from the questions given below:
options: Both statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is False.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II is false.
28521.sol:
The atomic and ionic radii, as we know, generally decrease in a period from left to right. As a consequence, the ionisation enthalpies generally increase (with some exceptions) and electron gain enthalpies become more negative across a period. In other words, the ionisation enthalpy of the extreme left element for a period is the least and the electron gain enthalpy of the element on the extreme right is the highest negative (Note: noble gases having completely filled shells have rather positive electron gain enthalpy values). This results in high chemical reactivity at the two extremes and the lowest in the centre. 


Group - 1 elements form basic nature oxides.  Metallic oxides are basic in nature because they react with dilute acids to form salt and water, while group - $17$ elements form acidic oxides, An oxide that exhibits the property of acids is called acidic oxide. Since they are acidic, they react with a base to form a salt. Non-metals react with oxygen to form acidic compounds of oxides which are held together by covalent bonds. Therefore, statement - II is true.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
30399.sol:
In the given Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction, $1$-chloropropane reacts with anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to initially form a primary carbocation, the $n$-propyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2^+$).

This primary carbocation is less stable and undergoes a $1,2$-hydride shift to form a more stable secondary carbocation, the iso-propyl carbocation ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}^+-\text{CH}_3$). Therefore, statement B is correct.

The iso-propyl carbocation then acts as an electrophile and attacks the benzene ring, yielding iso-propylbenzene (cumene) as the major product. Thus, statement A is incorrect.

Once an alkyl group is introduced to the benzene ring, it acts as an electron-donating group (via hyperconjugation and inductive effect), which activates the ring. This makes the newly formed alkylbenzene more reactive towards electrophilic aromatic substitution than the original benzene molecule, leading to polyalkylation. Hence, multiple substitution is a common and inevitable drawback. Therefore, statement C is correct.

Introducing an electron-donating substituent on benzene generally activates the ring and facilitates Friedel-Crafts alkylation (except for strong Lewis bases like $-\text{NH}_2$ which complex with $\text{AlCl}_3$). Thus, statement D is incorrect.

Therefore, only statements B and C are correct.

Answer: B and C only

$\begin{aligned}
& \lambda=900 \mathrm{ nm} \quad \text{ H-atom }(\mathrm{Z}=1) \\

& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}=\frac{1}{9}
\end{aligned}$

32921.text: The triangle of maximum area that can be inscribed in a given circle of radius '$r$' is :
options: An equilateral triangle having each of its side of length $\sqrt{3}r$.
An isosceles triangle with base equal to $2r$.
A right angle triangle having two of its sides of length $2r$ and $r$.
32921.sol:
$h = rsin\theta + r$

base $= BC = 2rcos\theta$

$\theta \in \left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Area of $\DeltaABC = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(BC\right) . h$

$\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2rcos\theta\right) . \left(rsin\theta + r\right)$

$= {r}^{2}\left(cos\theta\right) . \left(1 + sin\theta\right)$

$\dfrac{d\Delta}{d\theta} = {r}^{2}\left[cos\theta\dfrac{d}{d\theta}\left(1 + sin\theta\right) + \left(1 + sin\theta\right)\dfrac{d}{d\theta}\left(cos\theta\right)\right]$

$\dfrac{d\Delta}{d\theta} = {r}^{2}\left[cos\theta\left(0 + cos\theta\right) + \left(1 + sin\theta\right)\left(- sin\theta\right)\right]$

$\dfrac{d\Delta}{d\theta} = {r}^{2}\left[\cos^{2}\theta - sin\theta - \sin^{2}\theta\right]$

$\dfrac{d\Delta}{d\theta} = {r}^{2}\left[1 - \sin^{2}\theta - sin\theta - \sin^{2}\theta\right]$

$= {r}^{2}\left[1 - sin\theta - 2\sin^{2}\theta\right]$

$= {r}^{2}\left[- 2\sin^{2}\theta - sin\theta + 1\right]$

$= {r}^{2}\left[- 2\sin^{2}\theta - 2sin\theta + sin\theta + 1\right]$

$= {r}^{2}\left[- 2sin\theta\left(sin\theta + 1\right) + 1\left(sin\theta + 1\right)\right]$

$= \mathop{\mathop{{r}^{2}\left[1 + sin \theta\right]}_{⏟}}_{positive}\left[1 - 2sin\theta\right] = 0$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$⇒$ $\Delta$ is maximum where $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

${\Delta}_{max} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}{r}^{2} =$ area of equilateral $\Delta$ with $BC = \sqrt{3}r$.

34801.text: If $y = y\left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2ytanx = sinx, y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 0$, then the maximum value of the function $y\left(x\right)$ over $R$ is equal to :

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2ytanx = sinx$

$I . F . = {e}^{∫ 2tanxdx} = {e}^{2lnsecx}$

$I . F . = {sec}^{2}x$

$y . \left({sec}^{2}x\right) = ∫ sinx . {sec}^{2}xdx + C$

$y . \left({sec}^{2}x\right) = ∫ secxtanxdx + C$

Let $cosx = t, - 1 \le t \le 1$

$⇒ y = t - 2{t}^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dt} = 1 - 4t = 0 ⇒ t = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Second-order derivative is negative

$∴ max = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{2 - 1}{8} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

35637.text: The sum of possible values of $x$ for $\tan^{- 1}\left(x + 1\right) + {cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x - 1}\right) = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{8}{31}\right)$ is:
35637.sol:
Given $\tan^{- 1}\left(x + 1\right) + {cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x - 1}\right) = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{8}{31}$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(x + 1\right) + \tan^{- 1}\left(x - 1\right) = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{8}{31}, \left(∴ \tan^{- 1}x = {cot}^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{x}, x > 0\right)$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x + 1 + x - 1}{1 - \left(x + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)}\right) = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{8}{31}$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}\left[\dfrac{2x}{1 - \left(x + 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)}\right] = \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{8}{31}$

Taking tangent both the sides we get,

$\dfrac{( x + 1 ) + ( x - 1 )}{1 - \left({x}^{2} - 1\right)} = \dfrac{8}{31}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2x}{2 - {x}^{2}} = \dfrac{8}{31}$

$⇒ 4{x}^{2} + 31x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ x = - 8, \dfrac{1}{4}$

But, if $x = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$\tan^{- 1}\left(x + 1\right) \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

and ${cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x - 1}\right) \in \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)$

$⇒ LHS > \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $RHS < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ (Not possible)

Hence, $x = - 8 = - \dfrac{32}{4} .$

36039.text: Let A$ be a symmetric matrix such that \left|A\right|$= 2 and $\left[\begin{cases}2 & 1 \\ 3 &\dfrac{3}{2}$\end{cases}\right]$A = \left[$\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}$\right] If$ the sum of the diagonal elements of A is $s$, then $\dfrac{\betas}{{\alpha}^{2}}$ is equal to _________.
36039.sol:
Let

$A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ b & c\end{cases}\right]$

And,

$\left[\begin{cases}2 & 1 \\ 3 & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right]A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}2 & 1 \\ 3 & \dfrac{3}{2}\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ b & c\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}2a + b & 2b + c \\ 3a + \dfrac{3b}{2} & 3b + \dfrac{3c}{2}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ \alpha & \beta\end{cases}\right]$

So,

$2a + b = 12b + c = 2$

So, $4a - c = 0 . . . . \left(i\right)$

Also,

$\left|A\right| = 2 ⇒ ac - {b}^{2} = 2$

$⇒ a\left(4a\right) - {\left(1 - 2a\right)}^{2} = 2$

$⇒ 4{a}^{2} - 4{a}^{2} - 1 + 4a = 2$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ b = 1 - 2a = 1 - \dfrac{6}{4} = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$c = 4a = 3$

And,

$3a + \dfrac{3b}{2} = \alpha ⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{9}{4} - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}3b + \dfrac{3c}{2} = \beta ⇒ \beta = - \dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{9}{2} = 3$

So,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{4} & - \dfrac{1}{2} \\ - \dfrac{1}{2} & 3\end{cases}\right]$

So, $Tr\left(A\right) = s = \dfrac{3}{4} + 3 = \dfrac{15}{4}$

$\dfrac{\beta \times s}{{\alpha}^{2}} = \dfrac{3 \times \dfrac{15}{4}}{\dfrac{9}{4}} = 5$

36509.text: Two women and some men participated in a chess tournament in which every participant played two games with each of the other participants. If the number of games that the men played between them-selves exceeds the number of games that the men played with the women by$66$, then the number of men who participated in the tournament lies in the interval
36509.sol:
Let the number of men participating in tournament $= m$.

Number of women participating in tournament $= 2$.

Each player will play$2$ games with every other player and two women will play $2$ games with each man.

Total numbers of games played by women $= 2 \times 2m = 4m$

Total number of games played by men $= 2{\cdot}^{m}{C}_{2}$

From given data

$2{\cdot}^{m}{C}_{2} - 4m = 66$

$⇒ 2\dfrac{m\left(m - 1\right)}{2} - 4m = 66$

$⇒ {m}^{2} - 5m - 66 = 0$

$⇒ \left(m - 11\right)\left(m + 6\right) = 0$

$⇒ m = 11$ or $- 6$ but $m \in N, m \ne - 6$

$⇒ m \in \left[10, 12\right) .$

36923.text: The number of the real roots of the equation ${\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} + | x - 5 | = \dfrac{27}{4}$ is ________.
36923.sol:
Case-$I$

$x \le 5$

${\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} - \left(x - 5\right) = \dfrac{27}{4}$

${\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} - \left(x + 1\right) - \dfrac{3}{4} = 0$

$x + 1 = \dfrac{3}{2}, - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$x = \dfrac{1}{2}, - \dfrac{3}{2}$

Case-$II$

$x > 5$

$\left(x + 1\right) + \left(x - 5\right) = \dfrac{27}{4}$

${\left(x + 1\right)}^{2} + \left(x + 1\right) - \dfrac{51}{4} = 0$

$x = \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{52}}{2}$ (rejected as $x > 5$)

So, the equation have two real root.

38891.text: A $20$~$\text{H}$ inductor coil is connected to a $10Ω$& resistance in series as shown in figure. The time at which rate of dissipation of energy& (Joule's heat)& across resistance is equal to the rate at which magnetic energy is stored in the inductor, is:
38891.sol:
Rate of dissipation of energy in resistor $= {i}^{2}R$
Rate of energy stored in inductor $= \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}L{i}^{2}\right) = Li\dfrac{di}{dt}$
${i}^{2}R = Li\dfrac{di}{dt}$
$\dfrac{di}{dt} = i\dfrac{R}{L} \ldots \left(i\right)$
In $L - R$ circuit:

$i = {i}_{0}\left(1 - {e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}\right) ( ∴ τ = \dfrac{L}{R} = 2 )$
$\dfrac{di}{dt} = \dfrac{{i}_{0}}{τ}{e}^{- t / τ}$
From equation (i),

$\dfrac{{i}_{0}}{τ}{e}^{- t / τ} = {i}_{0}\left(1 - {e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}}\right)\dfrac{R}{L}$
${e}^{- t / τ} = 1 - {e}^{- t / τ}$
${e}^{- \dfrac{t}{τ}} = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ t = τln2$
$= 2ln2$

40737.text: In a Vernier calipers, when both jaws touch each other, zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the right of zero of the main scale and $7^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale reading. If the value of $1$ main scale division is $1$ mm and there are $10$ Vernier scale divisions, then the Vernier caliper has
40737.sol:
Least count of the Vernier calipers is given by $\text{LC} = \dfrac{1 \text{ MSD}}{\text{Number of VSD}}$.

Substituting the given values, $\text{LC} = \dfrac{1 \text{ mm}}{10} = 0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.01 \text{ cm}$.

Since the zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the right of the zero of the main scale, the zero error is positive.

The zero error is calculated as $+ (n \times \text{LC})$, where $n$ is the coinciding Vernier division.

Given that the $7^{\text{th}}$ Vernier division coincides with a main scale reading, $n = 7$.

Zero error $= + (7 \times 0.01 \text{ cm}) = + 0.07 \text{ cm}$.

Therefore, the Vernier caliper has a $0.07 \text{ cm}$ positive zero error.

Answer: $0.07$ cm positive zero error

43160.text: A uniform solid cylinder of length $L$ and radius $R$ has moment of inertia about its axis equal to $I_{1}$. A small co-centric cylinder of length $L / 2$ and radius $R / 3$ carved from this cylinder has moment of inertia about its axis equals to $I_{2}$. The ratio $I_{1} / I_{2}$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
43160.sol:
For solid cylinder: $I = \frac{1}{2}mR^2$
Large cylinder: mass $m_1 = \rho \pi R^2 L$, so $I_1 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^2 L \times R^2 = \frac{\rho \pi R^4 L}{2}$
Small cylinder (carved out): length L/2, radius R/3, mass $m_2 = \rho \pi(R/3)^2(L/2) = \frac{\rho \pi R^2 L}{18}$
$I_2 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\rho \pi R^2 L}{18} \times (R/3)^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{\rho \pi R^2 L}{18} \times \frac{R^2}{9} = \frac{\rho \pi R^4 L}{324}$
$\frac{I_1}{I_2} = \frac{\rho \pi R^4 L/2}{\rho \pi R^4 L/324} = \frac{324}{2} = 162$

46090.text: A ball of mass $m$ hits the floor with a speed $v$ making an angle of incidence $\theta$ with the normal. The coefficient of restitution is $e$. The speed of reflected ball and the angle of reflection of the ball will be
46090.sol:
The parallel component of velocity of the ball remains unchanged. This gives
$v^{\prime} \sin \theta^{\prime}=v \sin \theta$ ...(i)
For the components normal to the floor, the velocity of separation $=v^{\prime} \cos \theta^{\prime}$
and the velocity of approach $=v \cos \theta$
Hence, $\quad v^{\prime} \cos \theta^{\prime}=e v \cos \theta$ ... (ii)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii)
$\begin{aligned} v^{\prime} & =v \sqrt{\sin ^2 \theta+e^2 \cos ^2 \theta} \\ \text{ and } \quad \tan \theta^{\prime} & =\frac{\tan \theta}{e}\end{aligned}$
For elastic collision, $e=1$, so that $\theta^{\prime}=\theta$ and $v^{\prime}=v$

46177.subject: Physics
46177.text: If alpha, beta and gamma rays carry same momentum, which has the longest wavelength?
46177.sol:
On the basis of dual nature of light, Lious de-Broglie suggested that the dual nature is not only of light, but each moving material particle has the dual nature. He assumed a wave to be associated with each moving material particle which is called the matter wave. The wavelength of this wave is determined by the momentum of the particle. If $p$ is the momentum of the particle, the wavelength of the wave associated with it is
$\lambda=\frac{h}{p}$
where $h$ is Planck's constant.
Since, it is given that, alpha, beta and gamma rays carry same momentum, so they will have same wavelength.

55136.subject: Chemistry
55136.text: Which among the following has higher boiling point?
55136.sol:
Boiling points in a homologous series depend primarily on molecular weight and the resulting London dispersion forces. All aldehydes exhibit dipole-dipole interactions but cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

Molecular weights increase as follows: ethanal (2 carbons), propanal (3 carbons), pentanal (5 carbons), hexanal (6 carbons). With increasing molecular weight, surface area and dispersion forces strengthen, requiring more energy to vaporize.

Hexanal has the highest molecular weight and thus the strongest intermolecular forces, resulting in the highest boiling point.

55774.sol:
The dinitrogen molecule (N_2$) consists of two identical nitrogen atoms with symmetrical electron distribution, making it nonpolar.

Hydrogen bonding requires hydrogen attached to N, O, or F atoms. London dispersion forces arise from instantaneous electron fluctuations and operate in all molecular systems.

For nonpolar $N_2$, London dispersion forces constitute the only intermolecular interaction present.

The correct choice is \boxed{C}$.

56829.subject: Chemistry
56829.text: Which of the following solutions will have the highest electrical conductivity?
56829.sol:
Electrical conductivity of a solution depends on the concentration of free ions present in it.

Distilled water is a very poor conductor of electricity due to the negligible concentration of $H^+$ and $OH^-$ ions.

Sugar and alcohol are covalent compounds and do not dissociate into ions when dissolved in water. Hence, their solutions are non-electrolytes and do not conduct electricity.

Salt is an ionic compound and a strong electrolyte. It completely dissociates into its constituent ions in an aqueous solution, providing a large number of free ions for the conduction of electricity.

Thus, the salt solution will have the highest electrical conductivity.

Answer: Salt solution

58472.subject: Chemistry
58472.sol:
Thermocol, also known as expanded polystyrene (EPS), is a homopolymer. A homopolymer is a polymer that is composed of only one type of monomer unit repeated throughout its structure. In the case of thermocol, the repeating unit is the styrene monomer. When polymerized, styrene forms a long chain known as polystyrene, which is used in a variety of applications, including packaging materials like thermocol.
Here's a brief description of each option to clarify why the others are not homopolymers:
Polycarbonate (Option A): Polycarbonate is a copolymer commonly made from bisphenol A and phosgene, thus it's not a homopolymer.
Buna-N (Option B): Buna-N, also known as nitrile rubber, is a copolymer made from butadiene and acrylonitrile.
Glyptal (Option C): Glyptal is a copolymer derived from reaction between glycerol and phthalic anhydride, classifying it as a copolymer.

59094.text: Calculate the molar mass of nonelectrolyte solute when 6 gram of it is dissolved in 1 $\text{dm}^3$ water has osmotic pressure $2.4\ \text{atm}$ at 300 K $(R = 0.0821\ \text{atm dm}^3\ \textK^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1})$
59094.sol:
The osmotic pressure is given by the formula:

$\pi = C R T = \dfrac{W R T}{M V}$

Rearranging the formula to solve for the molar mass $M$:

$M = \dfrac{W R T}{\pi V}$

Substituting the given values $W = 6\ \text{g}$, $R = 0.0821\ \text{atm dm}^3\ \textK^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$, $T = 300\ \text{K}$, $\pi = 2.4\ \text{atm}$, and $V = 1\ \text{dm}^3$:

$M = \dfrac{6 \times 0.0821 \times 300}{2.4 \times 1}$

$M = \dfrac{147.78}{2.4}$

$M = 61.575\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to two decimal places, the molar mass is $61.58\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $61.58\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

59561.text: Four vessels of same volume consist equal moles of four gases $\mathrm{H}_2, \mathrm{Cl}_2$, $\mathrm{N}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$ separately at same temperature. The pressure exerted by the gas is maximum for -
59561.sol:
The gases demonstrate real behavior where pressure deviates from the ideal gas law due to intermolecular forces and molecular volume.

The van der Waals equation $P = \frac{nRT}{V - nb} - \frac{an^2}{V^2}$ governs this behavior, with $a$ representing intermolecular attraction and $b$ representing excluded volume.

For fixed $n$, $V$, and $T$, the compressibility factor $Z = \frac{PV}{nRT}$ approximates to $Z \approx 1 + \frac{n}{V} \left($b - $\frac{a}{RT}\right), making pressure maximization equivalent to maximizing \left($ b - $\frac{a}{RT}\right).

At $ T = 300$ K, using standard van der Waals constants:

\text{H}_2$: $0.0266 - \frac{0.244}{24.63} \approx +0.0167$
$\text{N}_2 : 0.0391 - \frac{1.39}{24.63} \approx -0.0173$
$\text{O}_2$ : 0.0318 - $\frac{1.36}{24.63}$ \approx -0.0234$
\text{Cl}_2 : 0.0562 - \frac{6.49}{24.63} \approx -0.2073$

Hydrogen yields the only positive value, indicating $Z > 1$ and maximum pressure among the gases.

$\boxed{A}$

59775.subject: Chemistry
59775.text: Which from following substances is classified as macromolecular colloid?
59775.sol:
Colloid classification depends on the dispersed phase particle structure. Multimolecular colloids form from aggregates of small molecules (e.g., gold sol), while macromolecular colloids consist of individual large molecules like proteins or synthetic polymers. Associated colloids (micelles) form aggregates only at higher concentrations, as with soaps.

Analyzing the options: soap and detergent form micelles (associated colloids), $\text{S}_8$ sulfur aggregates into multimolecular colloids, and nylon exists as individual macromolecules of colloidal size.

Nylon is therefore a macromolecular colloid.

59943.sol:
The standard enthalpy change, $\Delta_{\mathrm{r}} H^{{}^{\circ}}$, is calculated using the formula:

$\Delta_{\mathrm{r}} H^{{}^{\circ}} = \sum n \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} H^{{}^{\circ}}(\text{products}) - \sum m \Delta_{\mathrm{f}} H^{{}^{\circ}}(\text{reactants})$

60707.subject: Mathematics
60707.text: A circle passes through the point $(0,1)$ and touches the parabola $y = x^2$ at the point $(1,1)$. The centre of the circle is...
60707.sol:
The equation of the tangent to the parabola $y = x^2$ at the point $(1,1)$ is given by $T = 0$:

$\dfrac{y+1}{2} =$ x(1) \Rightarrow 2x - y - 1 = 0$

The equation of the family of circles touching the line 2x - y - 1 = 0$ at $(1,1)$ is:

$(x - 1)^2 + (y - 1)^2 + \lambda(2x - y - 1) = 0$

Since the circle passes through the point $(0,1)$, substituting $x = 0 and y = 1$ gives:

$(0 - 1)^2 + (1 - 1)^2 + \lambda(2(0) - 1 - 1) = 0$

$1 - 2\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Substituting $\lambda = \dfrac{1}{2}$ into the equation of the circle:

$(x - 1)^2 + (y - 1)^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}(2x - y - 1) = 0$

$x^2 - 2x + 1 + y^2 - 2y + 1 + x - \dfrac{y}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} = 0$

$x^2 + y^2 - x - \dfrac{5}{2}y + \dfrac{3}{2} = 0$

The coordinates of the centre of the circle $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ are $(-g, -f)$.

Centre $= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{5}{4}\right)

Answer: \left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{5}{4}\right)$

60923.text:
If $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is continuous at point $x=0$ where
$\mathrm{f}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}\frac{3 \sin x+5 \tan x}{a^x-1} & , x < 0 \\ \frac{2}{\log 2} & , x=0 \\ \frac{8 x+2 x \cos x}{\mathbf{b}^x-1} & , x > 0\end{array}\right.$
then the values of $a$ and b , respectively, are
60923.sol:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=0$ when $\lim_{x \to 0^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x) = f(0) = \frac{2}{\log 2}$, with $\log$ interpreted as the natural logarithm.

Evaluating the left-hand limit:

$\lim_{x \to 0^-} \frac{3 \sin x + 5 \tan x}{a^x - 1} = \lim_{x \to 0^-} \frac{\frac{3 \sin x}{x} + \frac{5 \tan x}{x}}{\frac{a^x - 1}{x}}$

Using standard limits $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin x}{x} = 1$, $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\tan x}{x} = 1$, and $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{a^x - 1}{x} = \ln a$, we obtain

$\frac{8}{\ln a}$.

For the right-hand limit:

$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \frac{8x + 2x \cos x}{b^x - 1} = \lim_{x \to 0^+} \frac{8 + 2 \cos x}{\frac{b^x - 1}{x}}$

Applying $\lim_{x \to 0} \cos x = 1$ and $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{b^x - 1}{x} = \ln b$ gives

$\frac{10}{\ln b}$.

Equating both limits to $f(0)$:

$\frac{8}{\ln a} = \frac{2}{\ln 2} \Rightarrow 8 \ln 2 = 2 \ln a \Rightarrow \ln a = 4 \ln 2 \Rightarrow a = 16$

$\frac{10}{\ln b} = \frac{2}{\ln 2} \Rightarrow 10 \ln 2 = 2 \ln b \Rightarrow \ln b = 5 \ln 2 \Rightarrow b = 32$

The values are $a = 16$ and $b = 32$, corresponding to option B.

63339.text: The equation $x^2-3 x y+\lambda y^2+3 x-5 y+2=0$, where $\lambda$ is real number, represents pair of lines. If $\theta$ is acute angle between the lines, then $\frac{\operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta}{\sqrt{10}}=$
63339.sol:
Using the condition for a pair of straight lines, the given equation satisfies $abc + 2fgh - af^2 - bg^2 - ch^2 = 0$. For $x^2 - 3xy + \lambda y^2 + 3x - 5y + 2 = 0$, the coefficients are $a=1$, $h=-\frac{3}{2}$, $g=\frac{3}{2}$, $b=\lambda$, $f=-\frac{5}{2}$, $c=2$.

Substituting into the condition:
$2\lambda + 2\left(\frac{-5}{2}\right)\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(\frac{-3}{2}\right) - 1\cdot\left(\frac{25}{4}\right) - \lambda\cdot\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) - 2\cdot\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) = 0$
$2\lambda + \frac{45}{4} - \frac{25}{4} - \frac{9\lambda}{4} - \frac{18}{4} = 0$
$2\lambda - \frac{9\lambda}{4} + \frac{2}{4} = 0$
$\frac{-\lambda + 2}{4} = 0$
$\lambda = 2$

For the acute angle $\theta$ between the lines, $\tan \theta = \left| \frac{2\sqrt{h^2 - ab}}{a + b} \right|$. With $a=1$, $b=2$, $h=-\frac{3}{2}$:
$h^2 - ab = \frac{9}{4} - 2 = \frac{1}{4}$
$\tan \theta = \left| \frac{2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}}{3} \right| = \frac{1}{3}$

Evaluating the trigonometric expression, $\frac{\csc^2 \theta}{\sqrt{10}} = \frac{1 + \cot^2 \theta}{\sqrt{10}}$. With $\cot \theta = 3$:
$\csc^2 \theta = 1 + 9 = 10$
$\frac{10}{\sqrt{10}} = \frac{10\sqrt{10}}{10} = \sqrt{10}$

The value is $\boxed{D}$.

66031.subject: Physics
66031.text: Two circular plates each of radius '$r$' are kept parallel to each other distance '$d$' apart. The capacitance of the capacitor formed is '$C_1$'. If the radius of each of the plates is increased to $\sqrt{3} times the earlier radius and their distance of separation decreased to half the initial value, the capacitance now becomes '$C_2$'. The ratio $C_1 : C_2$ is$
66031.sol:
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is given by $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$

For circular plates of radius $r$, the area is $A = \pi r^2$

Initial capacitance is $C_1 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 \pi r^2}{d}$

When the radius is increased to $\sqrt{3}r$, the new area is $A' = \pi (\sqrt{3}r)^2 = 3\pi r^2$

The new distance of separation is $d' = \dfrac{d}{2}$

The new capacitance is $C_2 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 (3\pi r^2)}{d/2} = \dfrac{6\epsilon_0 \pi r^2}{d}$

Taking the ratio of $C_1$ and $C_2$:

$\dfrac{C_1}{C_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\epsilon_0 \pi r^2}{d}}{\dfrac{6\epsilon_0 \pi r^2}{d}} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

The ratio $C_1 : C_2$ is $1 : 6$

Answer: $1 : 6$

68089.subject: Physics
68089.text: If we dip capillary tubes of different radii $r_n$ in water and the water rises to different heights $h_n$ in them, then (n = 1, 2, 3$.........)$
68089.sol:
The height $h$ of the liquid column in a capillary tube of radius $r$ is given by Jurin's law:

$h = \dfrac{2T \cos \theta}{\rho g r}$

For a given liquid and tube material, the surface tension $T$, angle of contact $\theta$, density $\rho$, and acceleration due to gravity $g$ are constants.

Therefore, $h \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$

$h r = \text{constant}$

For different capillary tubes, $h_n r_n = \text{constant}$.

Answer: $h_n r_n = \text{constant}$

68128.subject: Physics
68128.text: Three liquids have same surface tension and have densities $\rho_1, \rho_2$ and $\rho_3(\rho_1 > \rho_2 > \rho_3)$. In three identical capillaries rise of liquid is same. The corresponding angles of contact $\theta_1, \theta_2$ and $\theta_3$ are related as
68128.sol:
The height of capillary rise is given by the formula:

$h = \dfrac{2T \cos\theta}{r \rho g}$

Rearranging the formula for $\cos\theta$, we get:

$\cos\theta = \dfrac{h r g}{2T} \rho$

It is given that the surface tension $T$, capillary radius $r$, and capillary rise $h$ are the same for all three liquids. Therefore, the term $\dfrac{h r g}{2T}$ is a constant.

This implies that $\cos\theta \propto \rho$.

Given the relation between the densities is $\rho_1 > \rho_2 > \rho_3$, it follows that:

$\cos\theta_1 > \cos\theta_2 > \cos\theta_3$

For capillary rise, the angle of contact $\theta$ is acute ($0 \le \theta < 90^{}^{\circ}$). In this interval, the cosine function is strictly decreasing, meaning a larger value of $\cos\theta$ corresponds to a smaller angle $\theta$.

Thus, the relation between the angles of contact is:

$\theta_1 < \theta_2 < \theta_3$

Answer: $\theta_1 < \theta_2 < \theta_3$

68688.text: A point particle of mass 200 gram is executing S.H.M. of amplitude 0.2 m. When the particle passes through the mean position, its kinetic energy is $16 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ J}$. The equation of motion of this particle is (Initial phase of oscillation $=0^{{}^{\circ}}$ )
68688.sol:
Maximum kinetic energy in SHM relates to amplitude and angular frequency through the equation $KE_{\text\max} = \frac{1}{2} m (A\omega)^2$.

Substituting known values $m = 0.2\ \text{kg}$, $A = 0.2\ \text{m}$, and $KE_{\text\max} = 16 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{J}$:

$16 \times 10^{-3} = \frac{1}{2} (0.2) (0.2\omega)^2$

Solving for $\omega^2$:

$\omega^2 = \frac{16 \times 10^{-3}}{0.1 \times 0.04} = 4$

Thus $\omega = 2\ \text{rad/s}$.

The displacement equation becomes $Y = 0.2 \sin(2t)$, which corresponds to option D.

69462.sol:
The circuit output is given by $Y = (A + B)' \cdot C$.

For $Y = 1$, both $(A + B)'$ and $C$ must be 1. A NOR output equals 1 only when both inputs are 0, requiring $A = 0$ and $B = 0$. Combined with $C = 1$, this gives the condition for $Y = 1$.

Verifying the options: only $A = 0$, $B = 0$, $C = 1$ yields $Y = (0 + 0)' \cdot 1 = 1 \cdot 1 = 1$.
Therefore, the input that does not result in $Y = 0$ is option D.

70484.subject: Physics
70484.text: The fundamental frequency of a closed pipe is 400 Hz . If $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{\mathrm{rd}}$ length of the pipe is filled with water, the frequency of the $2^{\text{nd }}$ harmonic of the pipe will be (Neglect end correction)
70484.sol:
The fundamental frequency of a closed pipe is given by $f_1 = \frac{v}{4L}$, where $v$ is the speed of sound and $L$ is the pipe length.

Given $f_1 = 400$ Hz, we have $\frac{v}{4L} = 400$ Hz.

When $\frac{1}{3}$ of the pipe is filled with water, the effective air column length becomes $L' = \frac{2}{3}L$. The new fundamental frequency is $f_1' = \frac{v}{4L'} = \frac{v}{4(\frac{2}{3}L)} = \frac{3v}{8L}$.

Substituting $\frac{v}{4L} = 400$ Hz into the expression for $f_1'$ yields $f_1' = \frac{3}{2}(400) = 600$ Hz.

For a closed pipe, the harmonic frequencies are the odd multiples of the fundamental frequency. The second harmonic corresponds to $3f_1' = 3 \times 600 = 1800$ Hz.

Final answer: $\boxed{1800\ \text{Hz}}$

71511.subject: Biology
71511.text: In angiosperms, when the pollen tube enters the ovule through micropyle, it is called ______.
71511.sol:
In angiosperms, the entry of the pollen tube into the ovule can occur through different routes.

When the pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle, the process is known as porogamy. This is the most common type of pollen tube entry.

Chalazogamy refers to the entry of the pollen tube through the chalazal end.

Mesogamy refers to the entry of the pollen tube through the integuments or funiculus.

Siphonogamy is the general term for fertilization involving a pollen tube.

Answer: porogamy

71561.subject: Biology
71561.text: If any solute is added in pure water, what will be the effect on the value of water potential?
options: Value of water potential is increased.
Value of water potential is decreased.
There is no change in its value.
Value of water potential becomes more than D.P.D.
71561.sol:
Pure water has the maximum water potential, which is zero at standard temperature and pressure.

When a solute is added to pure water, the concentration of free water molecules decreases, which lowers the free energy of water.

This results in a decrease in the water potential, making it negative.

Therefore, the value of water potential is decreased.

Answer: Value of water potential is decreased.

71787.subject: Chemistry
71787.text:
Calculate the emf of the following cell at $25^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$
$\text{Zn(s)} \mid \text{Zn}^{++}(0.1\text{M}) \parallel \text{Cu}^{++}(0.05\text{M}) \mid \text{Cu(s)}$ if $E^{}^{\circ}$ cells 1.1V.
71787.sol:
The cell reaction is $\text{Zn(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Cu(s)}$

Number of electrons transferred, $n = 2$

Using the Nernst equation:

$E_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log \dfrac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]}$

Substituting the given values:

$E_{\text{cell}} = 1.1 - \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log \dfrac{0.1}{0.05}$

$E_{\text{cell}} = 1.1 - 0.02955 \log 2$

$E_{\text{cell}} = 1.1 - 0.02955 \times 0.3010$

$E_{\text{cell}} = 1.1 - 0.0089$

$E_{\text{cell}} = 1.0911 \text{ V}$

Answer: 1.091 V.

71973.subject: Chemistry
71973.text: Which of the following solutions has maximum vapour pressure?
71973.sol:
According to Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapour pressure is directly proportional to the concentration of the solute particles in the solution.

$\dfrac{P^0 - P_s}{P^0} \propto C$

This implies that the vapour pressure of the solution ($P_s$) is inversely proportional to the concentration of the solute.

Among the given options, the $0.01$ M copper sulphate solution has the minimum concentration. Therefore, it will have the minimum lowering of vapour pressure and consequently the maximum vapour pressure.

Answer: 0.01 M copper sulphate solution

72458.subject: Physics
72458.text: When light waves travel from rarer medium to denser medium, the qunatities which get changed are
72458.sol:
When light travels from one medium to another, the frequency of the light remains constant as it is a characteristic property of the source of light.

The velocity of light changes depending on the refractive index of the medium, given by $v = \dfrac{c}{\mu}$.

Since $v = \nu \lambda$ and the frequency $\nu$ is constant, the wavelength $\lambda$ must also change proportionally with the velocity.

Thus, velocity and wavelength change when light travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium.

Answer: velocity and wavelength.

72610.subject: General Ability
72610.text:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the items that follow the passage. Your answers to these items should be based solely on the passage.

Can agricultural productivity meet human needs in the long run? Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable, further increases in output will not be achieved easily. Global population growth, while showing signs of slowing down, has pushed farmers and herders into areas unsuited to intensive agriculture, accelerating worldwide ecological disruptions. Reserves of arable land and fresh water have diminished alarmingly. Chemical runoffs have compounded pollution problems. Invasion of natural habitats have hastened species extinction. Desertification has been severe in the last hundred years, especially in North Africa, southern portions of Africa, Australia, northern Mexico, and the American Southwest. Tropical forests have shrunk by one-half since World War II, with agricultural pressures causing three-quarters of that loss. Government intervention has produced its share of catastrophes, ranging from a terrible famine in China between 1958-1961 that may have killed 30 million people and destroyed the Aral Sea. Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century.

Why do twentieth century advances not seem sustainable?
options: They do not meet the human needs
Due to the increased cost of agricultural production
Because they are outdated for the current times
72610.sol:
According to the passage, the author states, "Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable, further increases in output will not be achieved easily."

This explicitly links the lack of sustainability of twentieth-century agricultural advances to the increasing costs associated with them.

Therefore, the correct reason is the increased cost of agricultural production.

Answer: Due to the increased cost of agricultural production

77215.text: If $x^a y^b=(x-y)^{a+b}$, then the value of $\frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{y}{x}$ is equal to
77215.sol:
$x^a y^b=(x-y)^{a+b}$
taking log both the sides.
$\begin{aligned}
& \log \left(x^a y^b\right)=\log (x-y)^{(a+b)} \\
& \text{ a logx }+b \operatorname{logy}=(a+b) \log (x-y) \\
& \text{ differentiating both sides w.r. }{ }^{\prime} x^{\prime} . \\
& \frac{a}{x}+\frac{b}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{(a+b)}{(x-y)}\left[1-\frac{d y}{d x}\right] \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}\left[\frac{b}{y}+\frac{a+b}{x-y}\right]=\frac{a+b}{x-y}-\frac{a}{x} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}\left[\frac{b x-b y+a y+b y}{y(x-y)}\right]=\frac{a x+b x-a x+}{x(x-y)} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}\left[\frac{b x+a y}{y}\right]=\frac{b x+a y}{x} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{x} \\
& \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{y}{x}=0
\end{aligned}$

77973.subject: Mathematics
77973.text:
Passage: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ be mutually exclusive and exhaustive events and $\dfrac{P(A)}{2}=\dfrac{P(B)}{3}=\dfrac{P(C)}{5}=\dfrac{P(D)}{8}$.

Question: What is $\dfrac{[2P(A)+3P(B)]}{[4P(C)+5P(D)]}$ equal to ?
77973.sol:
Let $\dfrac{P(A)}{2} = \dfrac{P(B)}{3} = \dfrac{P(C)}{5} = \dfrac{P(D)}{8} = k$

Then $P(A) = 2k$, $P(B) = 3k$, $P(C) = 5k$, and $P(D) = 8k$

Since $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are mutually exclusive and exhaustive events, $P(A) + P(B) + P(C) + P(D) = 1$

$2k + 3k + 5k + 8k = 1$

$18k = 1 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{1}{18}$

We need to evaluate $\dfrac{2P(A) + 3P(B)}{4P(C) + 5P(D)}$

Substituting the values in terms of $k$:

$\dfrac{2(2k) + 3(3k)}{4(5k) + 5(8k)} = \dfrac{4k + 9k}{20k + 40k} = \dfrac{13k}{60k} = \dfrac{13}{60}$

Answer: $\dfrac{13}{60}$

$\sin \mathrm{A}+2 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A}+\sin 3 \mathrm{~A}$ is equal to which of the following?
1. $4 \sin 2 \mathrm{~A} \cos ^2 \left(\frac{\mathrm{~A}}{2}\right)

79109.sol:
Let $\mathrm{A}=30^{{}^{\circ}}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow & \sin \mathrm{A}+2 \sin 2 \mathrm{ A}+\sin 3 \mathrm{ A}=\sin 30^{{}^{\circ}}+2 \sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}+\sin 90^{{}^{\circ}} \\

& \left(\because 2 \cos ^2 \mathrm{ A}=1+\cos 2 \mathrm{ A}\right)

& =2 \sin 2 \mathrm{ A}[1+\sin \mathrm{A}]=2 \sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}\left[1+\sin 30^{{}^{\circ}}\right] \\
& =\frac{3 \sqrt{3}}{2}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \& 8 \sin A \cos A \cos ^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{ A}}{2}\right) \\
& =4 \sin \mathrm{ A} \cos \mathrm{ A}[1+\cos \mathrm{A}] \\
& =4 \sin 30^{{}^{\circ}} \cos 30^{{}^{\circ}}\left[1+\cos 30^{{}^{\circ}}\right] \\
& =\frac{2 \sqrt{3}+3}{2}
\end{aligned}$

80944.subject: Chemistry
80944.text: The correct sequence of increasing covalent character is represented by:
80944.sol:
According to Fajan's Rule,
1. Smaller the size of cation, the larger the size of the anion, greater is the covalent character of the ionic bond.
2. Greater the charge of cation, greater is the covalent character of the ionic bond.
3. For cations with same charge and size, the one, with $(n-1) d^n n s^{{}^{\circ}}$ which is found in transition elements have greater covalent character than the cation with $n s^2 n p^6$ electronic configuration, which is commonly found in alkali or alkaline earth metals.
Thus, order of covalent character is:

$\mathrm{NaCl}$< $\mathrm{LiCl}$<  $\mathrm{BeCl}_{2}

I Caution
Larger the anion, less is the effective nuclear charge that holds the valence electron of the ion in place. Since the last electron is loosely bound in large anions, it can easily be polarised by a cation, thereby making the compound more covalent.$

81548.subject: Chemistry
81548.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I:
trans-But-2-ene upon treatment with Br$_2$ in CCl$_4$ gives the following product

Statement II:
cis-But-2-ene upon treatment with alkaline KMnO$_4$ gives the following product

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
81548.sol:
Reaction of trans-but-2-ene with Br$_2$ in CCl$_4$ proceeds via anti-addition to give meso-2,3-dibromobutane.

In the Newman projection given in Statement I, the front carbon has Br at $0^{\circ}$, Me at $120^{\circ}$, and H at $240^{\circ}$. The back carbon has Br at $180^{\circ}$, Me at $60^{\circ}$, and H at $300^{\circ}$. For this staggered conformation to be meso, it must have a center of inversion, meaning a group at angle $\theta$ on the front carbon must have an identical group at $\theta + 180^{\circ}$ on the back carbon. While the Br atoms are opposite ($0^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$), the front Me at $120^{\circ}$ is not opposite to the back Me at $60^{\circ}$. Thus, it lacks a center of inversion and represents a chiral enantiomer. Hence, Statement I is incorrect.

Reaction of cis-but-2-ene with alkaline KMnO$_4$ proceeds via syn-addition to give meso-butane-2,3-diol.

In the Newman projection given in Statement II, the front carbon has OH at $0^{\circ}$, Me at $120^{\circ}$, and H at $240^{\circ}$. The back carbon has OH at $60^{\circ}$, Me at $180^{\circ}$, and H at $300^{\circ}$. Rotating the back carbon by $60^{\circ}$ counter-clockwise perfectly eclipses all identical groups (OH with OH at $0^{\circ}$, Me with Me at $120^{\circ}$, H with H at $240^{\circ}$). This indicates the presence of a plane of symmetry, confirming it is the meso isomer. Hence, Statement II is correct.

Therefore, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

82541.subject: Physics
82541.text: A ray of light with wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on three different photo-electric cells namely 1, 2 and 3. The threshold wavelength of these photo-electric cells are $\lambda_1$, $\lambda_2$, and $\lambda_3$, respectively and the magnitude of stopping potentials of these cells are $V_1$, $V_2$ and $V_3$, respectively. The relation between $\lambda$ and threshold wavelengths are $\lambda_1<\lambda$, $\lambda_2>\lambda$ and $\lambda_3\gg\lambda$. The correct option is :
82541.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the magnitude of the stopping potential $V$ is given by:

$eV = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{th}}$

For photoelectric emission to take place, the incident wavelength $\lambda$ must be less than the threshold wavelength $\lambda_{th}$.

For cell 1, $\lambda > \lambda_1$. No photoelectric emission occurs, so $V_1 = 0$.

For cell 2, $\lambda < \lambda_2$. Photoelectric emission occurs, and $V_2 = \dfrac{hc}{e} \left( \dfrac{1}{\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_2} \right) > 0$.

For cell 3, $\lambda \ll \lambda_3$. Photoelectric emission occurs, and $V_3 = \dfrac{hc}{e} \left( \dfrac{1}{\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_3} \right) > 0$.

Since $\lambda_3 \gg \lambda$ and $\lambda_2 > \lambda$, it follows that $\lambda_3 > \lambda_2$, which gives $\dfrac{1}{\lambda_3} < \dfrac{1}{\lambda_2}$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_3} > \dfrac{1}{\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_2}$, which implies $V_3 > V_2$.

Thus, $V_1 = 0$ and $V_2 < V_3$.

Answer: $V_1=0,\,V_2 < V_3$

85499.subject: Zoology
85499.text: If the head of cockroach is removed, it may live for few days because
options: the cockroach does not have nervous system.
the head holds a small proportion of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral part of its body.
the head holds a 1/3<sup>rd</sup> of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the dorsal part of its body.
the supra-oesophageal ganglia of the cockroach are situated in ventral part of abdomen.
85499.sol:
NERVOUS SYSTEM:

The nervous system of the cockroach consists of a series of fused, segmentally arranged ganglia joined by paired longitudinal connectives on the ventral side.

Brain: It is present in the head. It is made up of a pair of supra oesophageal which is the present above esophagus. It supplies nerves to antennae and compound eyes. The sub-oesophageal ganglia are present below the esophagus. These ganglions are connected together by paired longitudinal connectives on the ventral side.

Double Ventral Nerve Cord: They arise from sub-oesophageal ganglia and run-up to the posterior end of the body. These nerve cords are connected with the help of 9 pairs of segmented ganglion three in the thorax and 6 in the abdominal segment.

The nervous system of cockroaches is spread throughout the body. The head holds a bit of the nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral side of the body.

89243.text: $\text{100}\text{g}$ of liquid $\text{A}$ (molar mass $\text{140}\text{g}{\text{mol}}^{- \text{1}}$) was dissolved in $\text{1000}\text{g}$ of liquid $\text{B}$ (molar mass $\text{180}\text{g}{\text{mol}}^{- \text{1}}$). The vapour pressure of pure liquid $\text{B}$ was found to be $\text{500}\text{torr}$. Calculate vapour pressure of $\text{A}$~(in torr) the solution if the total vapour pressure of the solution is $\text{475}\text{torr}\text{.}$
89243.sol:
Step I : Calculation of vapour pressure of pure liquid A (p°A)
​Number of moles of liquid A
$\left({\text{n}}_{\text{A}}\right) = \dfrac{{\text{W}}_{\text{A}}}{{\text{M}}_{\text{A}}} = \dfrac{\text{(100 g)}}{\left({\text{140 g mol}}^{- 1}\right)} = \text{0.7143 mol}$
Number of moles of liquid B
$\left({\text{n}}_{\text{B}}\right) = \dfrac{{\text{W}}_{\text{B}}}{{\text{M}}_{\text{B}}} = \dfrac{\text{(1000 g)}}{\left({\text{180 g mol}}^{- 1}\right)} = \text{5.5556 mol}$
Mole fraction of A
$\left({\text{x}}_{\text{A}}\right) = \dfrac{{\text{n}}_{\text{A}}}{{\text{n}}_{\text{A}} + {\text{n}}_{\text{B}}}$
$= \dfrac{\text{(0.7143 mol)}}{\text{(0.7143 + 5.5556) mol}} = \dfrac{\text{0.7143}}{\text{6.2699}} = \text{0.1139}$
Mole fraction of ${\text{B(x}}_{\text{B}} \text{)}\text{=}1 - 0.1139 = 0.8861$
Vapour pressure of pure liquid B, ${\text{B(p}}_{\text{B}}^{\text{o}} \text{)}\text{=}\text{500}\text{torr}$
Total vapour pressure of solution $\text{(p)} = 475\text{torr}$
According to the Raoult's law
$\text{p}\text{=}{\text{p}}_{\text{A}}^{\text{o}} {\text{x}}_{\text{A}} \text{+}{\text{p}}_{\text{B}}^{\text{o}} {\text{x}}_{\text{B}}$
$\text{475}\text{torr}\text{=}{\text{p}}_{\text{A}}^{\text{o}} \text{\times}\text{(0}\text{.1139)}\text{+}\text{500}\text{torr}\text{\times}\text{(0}\text{.8861)}$
$\text{475}\text{torr}\text{=}{\text{p}}_{\text{A}}^{\text{o}} \text{\times}\text{(0}\text{.1139)}\text{+}\text{443}\text{.05}\text{torr}$
${\text{p}}_{\text{A}}^{\text{o}} = \dfrac{\left(\text{475} - \text{443.05}\right) \text{torr}}{\text{(0.1139)}} = \dfrac{\text{31.95}}{\text{0.1139}} \text{torr} = \text{280.5 torr}$

Step II : Calculation of vapour pressure of A in the solution (pA)
According to Raoult's law,
${\text{p}}_{\text{A}} \text{=}{\text{p}}_{\text{A}}^{\text{o}} {\text{x}}_{\text{A}} \text{=}\text{(280}\text{.5}\text{torr)}\text{\times}\text{(0}\text{.1139)}$
${\text{p}}_{\text{A}} \text{=}\text{32}\text{.0}\text{torr}$

Since, power of $a$ and $b$ are the same
$⇒ \dfrac{21 - r}{3} - \dfrac{r}{6} = \dfrac{r}{3} - \dfrac{21 - r}{3}$
$⇒ \dfrac{2\left(21 - r\right)}{3} = \dfrac{r}{3} + \dfrac{r}{6} = \dfrac{r}{2}$

The general equation of the family is ${x}^{2} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} = 1 \ldots \ldots . . \left(i\right)$
Differentiating w.r.t. $x,$ we get $2x + \dfrac{2y{y}^{'}}{{a}^{2}} = 0$
$⇒ x = - \dfrac{{y}^{′} y}{{a}^{2}} ⇒ {a}^{2} = - \dfrac{{y}^{′}}{x}$
Putting in (i), we have ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} \left(- \dfrac{x}{y{y}^{′}}\right) = 1$
or ${x}^{2} - \dfrac{xy}{{y}^{′}} = 1$
Which is of the degree $‘1’$

91585.text: A biased coin that has a probability of getting heads as $p$ $( 0 < p < 1 )$ is tossed until a head appears for the first time. If the probability that the number of tosses required is even, is $\dfrac{2}{5}$, then $9p$ is equal to
91585.sol:
$p:$ probability of getting head

$q:$ probability of getting tail

Such that, $p + q = 1$

According to question we can get head in ${2}^{nd}, {4}^{th}, {6}^{th}$ … tail.

Hence required probability $= qp\left(1 + {q}^{2} + {q}^{4} + \ldots\right) = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒$ $\dfrac{qp}{1 - {q}^{2}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$⇒ 5pq = 2 - 2{q}^{2}$

$⇒ 5p( 1 - p ) = 2 - 2{( 1 - p )}^{2}$

$⇒ 5p - 5{p}^{2} = 2 - 2( 1 + {p}^{2} - 2p )$

$⇒ 5p - 5{p}^{2} = 2 - 2 - 2{p}^{2} + 4p$

$⇒ 3{p}^{2} = p$

$⇒ p( 3p - 1 ) = 0$

$⇒ p = 0, p = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$∵ p \ne 0$

$∴ p = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ 9p = 3$

100668.subject: Physics
100668.text: Two masses of $3\text{ kg}$ and $2\text{ kg}$ are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest. What is the distance travelled by the heavier mass in the first $2\text{ seconds}$? (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
100668.sol:
The acceleration $a$ of an Atwood machine with masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ ($m_1 > m_2$) is given by:
$a = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$

Substituting the given values ($m_1 = 3\text{ kg}$, $m_2 = 2\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
$a = \dfrac{3 - 2}{3 + 2} \times 10 = \dfrac{1}{5} \times 10 = 2\text{ m/s}^2$

The system starts from rest, so initial velocity $u = 0$. The distance $s$ travelled in time $t = 2\text{ s}$ is:
$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2$
$s = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (2)^2$
$s = 4\text{ m}$

Answer: $4\text{ m}$

101398.subject: Physics
101398.text: An object is released from a height $h_1 = 3R_E$ above the surface of the earth, where $R_E$ is the radius of the earth. As it falls, it reaches a height $h_2$ above the earth's surface where its weight becomes $4$ times its weight at the release point. The value of $h_2$ is:
101398.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ from the surface of the earth is given by $g_h = g \left(\dfrac{R_E}{R_E + h}\right)^2$.

At the initial height $h_1 = 3R_E$, the acceleration due to gravity is:
$g_1 = g \left(\dfrac{R_E}{R_E + 3R_E}\right)^2 = g \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^2 = \dfrac{g}{16}$

The weight of the object at this height is $W_1 = m g_1 = \dfrac{mg}{16}$.

At height $h_2$, the weight becomes $4$ times the initial weight:
$W_2 = 4 W_1 = 4 \times \dfrac{mg}{16} = \dfrac{mg}{4}$

This means the acceleration due to gravity at $h_2$ is $g_2 = \dfrac{g}{4}$.

Using the formula for $g$ at height $h_2$:
$\dfrac{g}{4} = g \left(\dfrac{R_E}{R_E + h_2}\right)^2$

Taking the square root on both sides:
$\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{R_E}{R_E + h_2}$

$R_E + h_2 = 2R_E$

$h_2 = R_E$

Thus, the height $h_2$ is $R_E$.

Answer: $R_E$

102938.subject: Physics
102938.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a uniformly charged solid conducting sphere of radius $R$, the electric field at a distance $r$ ($r > R$) from the center is given by $\dfrac{VR}{r^2}$, where $V$ is the potential on the surface.

Reason (R): The electric potential at a distance $r > R$ from the center is given by $V(r) = V\left(\dfrac{R^2}{r^2}\right)$, and the electric field is the negative gradient of the potential.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
102938.sol:
Assertion is true: The potential on the surface of the conducting sphere is $V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q}{R}$. The electric field outside the sphere at distance $r > R$ is $E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q}{r^2}$. Substituting $q = 4\pi\varepsilon_0 V R$ into the electric field expression gives $E = \dfrac{V R}{r^2}$.

Reason is false: The electric potential outside the sphere at a distance $r > R$ is $V(r) = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q}{r}$. In terms of surface potential $V$, this is $V(r) = V\left(\dfrac{R}{r}\right)$, not $V\left(\dfrac{R^2}{r^2}\right)$. The electric field is indeed the negative gradient of the potential ($E = -\dfrac{dV}{dr}$), but the expression for $V(r)$ given in the reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

103336.subject: Physics
103336.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding a uniform wire of initial resistance $R_0$ undergoing various modifications. The equivalent resistance in each case is $R_{eq}$.

List-IList-II
(A) Stretched to twice its length, bent into a circle, measured across a diameter(I) $\dfrac{R_{eq}}{R_0} = 1$
(B) Stretched to three times its length, bent into an equilateral triangle, measured across one side(II) $\dfrac{R_{eq}}{R_0} = 2$
(C) Stretched to twice its length, cut into 4 equal parts, all connected in parallel(III) $\dfrac{R_{eq}}{R_0} = \dfrac{1}{4}$
(D) Stretched to four times its length, bent into a square, measured across adjacent corners(IV) $\dfrac{R_{eq}}{R_0} = 3$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
103336.sol:
When a wire is stretched to $n$ times its original length, its resistance becomes $n^2 R_0$.

(A) Stretched to $2l$: $R_{new} = 4 R_0$. Bent into a circle, the two halves across a diameter are in parallel. Each half has resistance $2 R_0$.
$R_{eq} = \dfrac{2 R_0 \times 2 R_0}{2 R_0 + 2 R_0} = R_0$. Ratio = $1$. (A $\rightarrow$ I)

(B) Stretched to $3l$: $R_{new} = 9 R_0$. Bent into an equilateral triangle, each side has resistance $3 R_0$. Across one side, one branch has $3 R_0$ and the other has $6 R_0$ (two sides in series).
$R_{eq} = \dfrac{3 R_0 \times 6 R_0}{3 R_0 + 6 R_0} = 2 R_0$. Ratio = $2$. (B $\rightarrow$ II)

(C) Stretched to $2l$: $R_{new} = 4 R_0$. Cut into 4 equal parts, each part has resistance $R_0$. Connecting 4 such parts in parallel gives:
$R_{eq} = \dfrac{R_0}{4}$. Ratio = $\dfrac{1}{4}$. (C $\rightarrow$ III)

(D) Stretched to $4l$: $R_{new} = 16 R_0$. Bent into a square, each side has resistance $4 R_0$. Across adjacent corners, one branch has $4 R_0$ and the other has $12 R_0$ (three sides in series).
$R_{eq} = \dfrac{4 R_0 \times 12 R_0}{4 R_0 + 12 R_0} = 3 R_0$. Ratio = $3$. (D $\rightarrow$ IV)

The correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)
